vendors.name: Snyk Open Source
vendors.offering: Developer-first SCA with fix PRs for direct and transitive dependencies
vendors.pricing: Free tier (200 OSS tests); Team $25/contributing dev/month, 5-dev minimum; Enterprise custom

vendors.name: GitHub Code Security (Dependabot)
vendors.offering: Dependabot alerts/updates plus premium dependency review bundled into GitHub
vendors.pricing: Code Security $30/active committer/month; basic Dependabot included with GitHub

vendors.name: Mend Renovate Enterprise / Mend SCA
vendors.offering: Automated dependency update PRs incl. transitive deps, merge confidence, SaaS or self-hosted
vendors.pricing: Renovate from $25,000/yr for 100 devs; Mend SCA from $18,000/yr for 25 devs (possibly stale page)

vendors.name: Endor Labs
vendors.offering: SCA with function-level reachability and upgrade impact analysis to cut noise

vendors.name: Socket
vendors.offering: Dependency supply-chain security: malicious package detection and vulnerable dependency alerts
vendors.pricing: Free tier; Team about $25/dev/month, 5-dev minimum (third-party reports)

vendors.name: Semgrep Supply Chain
vendors.offering: SCA with reachability analysis bundled with Semgrep code scanning

vendors.name: Aikido Security
vendors.offering: All-in-one AppSec platform incl. SCA with reachability and AutoFix
vendors.pricing: Free for 2 users; paid from about $300-350/month for 10 users (sources conflict)

vendors.name: Seal Security
vendors.offering: Backported patched library versions for unfixable or transitive vulnerable dependencies

paid_market_gaps.gap: Transitive vulns blocked by parent version ranges or missing lockfile entries get no automatic fix PR
Per-developer pricing causes sticker shock as teams grow to 30-50 developers
Reachability and AutoFix locked to paid/enterprise tiers; free tiers only alert
No policy to fast-track security fixes past release-age cooldowns used against supply-chain attacks

wtp_evidence: Many vendors publish $25-40/developer/month SCA prices and Mend lists $25k/yr Renovate deals; buyers pay, but switch on price and free Dependabot sets a low baseline.
bundling_note: GitHub includes Dependabot alerts and security updates with the platform and sells Code Security add-ons, so baseline detect-and-bump is effectively free.
summary: Crowded, bundled market; no opening for another scanner. Narrow wedge: fixing the stuck cases (transitive conflicts, no-fix CVEs, cooldown-bypass policy) sold to teams already paying Snyk/GitHub, but Seal and Endor already target this.

vendors.name: Anchore Enterprise
vendors.offering: SBOM generation and management with vulnerability scanning, risk scoring and VEX annotations

vendors.name: Manifest
vendors.offering: SBOM and VEX management separating theoretical CVEs from actual product exposure

vendors.name: Interlynk
vendors.offering: SBOM management and vulnerability tracking across products
vendors.pricing: not public; priced by active developer count, free trial

vendors.name: Cybeats SBOM Studio
vendors.offering: SBOM aggregation, vulnerability disposition workflow, VEX import/generation and sharing
vendors.pricing: not public; subscription by monitored SBOMs/products, not seats

vendors.name: Finite State
vendors.offering: Build-derived SBOMs enriched with exploit context, VEX and CRA compliance packages

vendors.name: JFrog Xray (Transitive SBOM)
vendors.offering: Dependency graph tree view showing direct vs transitive components from artifacts/SBOMs

vendors.name: ArmorCode
vendors.offering: Continuous SBOM and VEX management for CRA product manufacturers

vendors.name: ONEKEY
vendors.offering: Firmware SBOM and vulnerability analysis with compliance mapping, Dependency-Track alternative

paid_market_gaps.gap: Teams on free Dependency-Track lack parent-component, container and vendor-advisory context; commercial tools are enterprise quote-only
Dependency-Track has no vendor-managed cloud with support and no reachability; no affordable hosted upgrade path
Ingesting vendor CSAF advisories to match against SBOMs is missing in common tooling
Transitive dependency graph views only work on some input types (bundled artifacts)

wtp_evidence: Several funded SBOM/VEX vendors sell quote-based subscriptions; CRA reporting duties live since Sept 2026 push manufacturers to buy, but prices are not public and demand framing is mostly vendor-sourced.
bundling_note: AWS Inspector exports SBOMs free and JFrog/SCA suites add graph views, but cross-vendor VEX/CSAF product-impact analysis is not given away by clouds.
summary: Real but competitive opening: an affordable hosted SBOM impact/VEX layer (CSAF ingestion, dependency paths, container mapping) for mid-size software and device vendors facing CRA, positioned above free Dependency-Track and below enterprise quote-only platforms.
